chunks: Retrieval-augmented generation pairs a pretrained language model with a retriever that looks up passages from an external index.
The retriever encodes the question and each passage as vectors and picks the passages whose vectors are closest.
Grounding answers in retrieved text makes them easier to verify and cuts down on made-up facts.
The model can be updated by swapping its index, without retraining any weights.
The approach was evaluated on open-domain question answering, question generation and fact verification.
Results improved over models that rely only on knowledge stored in their parameters.
answer:
**Retrieval-augmented generation** answers a question by first looking up relevant passages, then writing a response grounded in them.

- It retrieves passages from an external index
- It can point to where each claim came from
